title: Japanese Sweet Potato Wedges
description: Naturally sweet and perfectly soft — a classic first BLW finger food beloved by babies across Japan. No seasoning needed.

steps.instruction: Preheat oven to 200°C (400°F).
Scrub the sweet potato well and leave the skin on for easy gripping.
steps.tip: The skin acts as a natural handle for little hands.

steps.instruction: Cut into thick wedges, about the size of two adult fingers placed side by side.
Place on a baking tray lined with parchment paper. Drizzle with a tiny amount of oil (optional).
Bake for 25–30 minutes until soft all the way through. A fork should pierce easily with no resistance.
steps.tip: Always test the inside. The outside softens quickly but the inside must be fully cooked.

steps.instruction: Let cool until warm to the touch before serving.
steps.tip: Never serve hot food directly from the oven.

safetyNotes: Ensure wedges are fully soft before serving. Always test temperature. Supervise during feeding.
storageReheatingNotes: Store in fridge for up to 3 days. Reheat in oven or microwave until warm throughout.
creatorNotes: My daughter Hana loved these from 6 months. They're her favourite grab-and-gnaw food!

title: West African Groundnut Stew (Baby Version)
description: A mild, protein-rich peanut-based stew inspired by West African groundnut soup. This baby-friendly adaptation removes chilli and salt. Rich in iron from chicken and healthy fats from groundnuts.

ingredients.name: Chicken thigh (boneless, skinless)
ingredients.notes: shredded into soft strips after cooking

ingredients.name: Unsalted smooth peanut butter
ingredients.notes: 100% peanuts, no added salt or sugar

steps.instruction: Heat coconut oil in a pot over medium heat. Add diced onion and garlic. Cook until soft, about 3 minutes.
Add blended tomatoes and cook for 5 minutes, stirring, until reduced.
Add chicken pieces and diced sweet potato. Stir to combine.
Add water or stock. Bring to a simmer, cover and cook for 20 minutes.
Stir in peanut butter until fully dissolved. Simmer uncovered for 5 more minutes until the stew thickens.
steps.tip: If too thick, add a splash more water.

steps.instruction: Remove chicken and shred into small, manageable strips. Return to pot.
Cool to a safe temperature. Serve with soft pounded yam or mashed sweet potato.

chokingHazardNotes: Shred chicken finely and ensure sweet potato is very soft. Check for bones.
safetyNotes: Contains peanuts. Do not introduce peanuts without first checking with your pediatrician if there is a family history of allergies. Introduce peanuts early according to LEAP study guidance.
storageReheatingNotes: Freeze portions for up to 1 month. Reheat thoroughly until piping hot, then cool before serving.
creatorNotes: This is a simplified version of what my mother made in Accra. I've been making it for my son Kwame since he was 7 months. He claps when he sees the pot!

title: Turkish Lentil Kofta (Mercimek Köfte) for Baby
description: A traditional Turkish cold appetiser made entirely from red lentils and bulgur wheat. Naturally vegan, high in plant protein and fibre, and incredibly easy to make into soft little balls for baby fingers.

steps.instruction: Cook red lentils in 1 cup of water for 15–18 minutes until completely soft and mushy. Drain any excess water.
While lentils are still hot, add bulgur wheat and mix well. Cover and let sit for 10 minutes — the steam will cook the bulgur.
steps.tip: The mixture should form a dough-like consistency.

steps.instruction: Add olive oil and tomato paste. Mix thoroughly.
Add minced onion, cumin, and parsley. Knead together well.
Shape into small oval patties or finger-sized rolls. Cool completely before serving.
steps.tip: Baby portion: flatten slightly so they don't roll away on the tray.

safetyNotes: Contains gluten (bulgur wheat). Not suitable for coeliacs. Ensure fully cooled before serving.
storageReheatingNotes: Refrigerate for 3 days or freeze for 1 month. Serve cold or at room temperature — traditional Turkish style!
creatorNotes: Köfte is a staple at my family table in Izmir. I make these every week — my 10-month-old son eats four in one sitting!

title: Indian Moong Dal Pancakes (Cheela) for Baby
description: Cheela is a traditional Indian savoury crepe made from yellow moong dal. High in plant-based protein, easy to digest, and perfect for baby hands to grip and self-feed.

steps.instruction: Blend soaked moong dal with a small splash of water into a smooth, thick batter.
Stir in grated vegetables, cumin seeds, and coriander. Mix well.
Heat a non-stick pan over medium heat. Add a few drops of oil or ghee.
Pour 2–3 tablespoons of batter and spread gently into a circle, like a small crepe.
steps.tip: For BLW, make slightly thicker pancakes than traditional cheela so baby can grip easily.

steps.instruction: Cook 2–3 minutes until the bottom is golden and edges lift. Flip and cook 1–2 more minutes.
Cool and cut into strips for easy self-feeding.

safetyNotes: Ensure pancakes are soft and fully cooked through. Test temperature before serving.
storageReheatingNotes: Store in fridge for 2 days. Warm gently in a pan. Can be frozen between layers of baking paper.
creatorNotes: Cheela is what I grew up eating in Delhi. My mother made it for us every weekend. Now I make it for my 7-month-old Arjun and he loves holding the strips!

title: Mexican Avocado & Black Bean Toast
description: A simple, nutrient-dense first food inspired by Mexican flavours. Healthy fats from avocado, plant protein from black beans, all on soft toast that dissolves easily.

steps.instruction: Mash avocado and black beans together with a fork until well combined but not completely smooth — a little texture helps babies learn.
Add a few drops of lime juice and a tiny pinch of cumin if using.
Toast bread until soft (not crunchy). Remove crusts if still hard.
steps.tip: For babies under 9 months, use very soft bread that compresses easily between your fingers.

steps.instruction: Spread avocado mixture generously on toast.
Cut into long finger-shaped strips for easy self-feeding.

safetyNotes: Ensure toast is soft, not crunchy. Avocado is a great first food for its fat content. Test for wheat/gluten tolerance first.
storageReheatingNotes: Best served fresh. Avocado browns quickly — add lime juice to slow oxidation.
creatorNotes: In my family in Oaxaca, avocado is on everything! I was so excited to share this tradition with my daughter from her very first bite.
